headline: Authorities identify dead, missing men after Manchester-by-the-Sea boat crash
dek: Carl Potter of Beverly died after a boat went into distress off Singing Beach, while Hamilton resident James Wolcott remained missing and a third man was hospitalized.
body: Authorities have identified the man who died and the man who remained missing after Saturday’s boating incident off Manchester-by-the-Sea. The Essex County District Attorney’s Office identified the victim as Carl Potter, 67, of Beverly, and the missing boater as James Wolcott, 37, of Hamilton, according to [NBC Boston](https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/manchester-by-sea-mass-boat-crash-update/4026037/) and [Boston.com](https://www.boston.com/news/local-news/2026/10/05/manchester-by-the-sea-boat-crash-victims-identified/). A third man, 65, remained hospitalized and was not publicly identified.

The three men and a dog were aboard a boat that went into distress off Singing Beach on Saturday, Oct. 3. The Manchester-by-the-Sea Police Department said the Coast Guard received the initial report at about 4:30 p.m., after which the passengers entered the water. Two men and the dog were located, one man died and the third passenger remained missing. The department’s account lists a broad response that included Coast Guard units, Massachusetts State Police, local harbor departments, the Beverly Fire Department dive team, Gloucester police and Massachusetts Environmental Police: [Manchester-by-the-Sea police](https://manchestermapd.com/manchester-by-the-sea-public-safety-responds-to-boat-crash/).

The reported sequence of the crash remains preliminary. [Boston 25 News](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/authorities-identify-man-killed-missing-boater-after-manchester-by-the-sea-accident/NOS4XSML5VFOVGA7PKEGVQNLXU/) said the Coast Guard received reports that the boat was spinning out of control and had struck rocks. Crews arrived around 4:48 p.m. and launched a 29-foot response boat. Boston.com, citing a Coast Guard spokesperson, likewise reported that the vessel struck rocks and spun out of control. Those accounts describe the emergency response but do not establish a final cause.

Rescuers pulled Potter from the water and brought him to Beverly Hospital, where he was pronounced dead, NBC Boston reported. The 65-year-old man was flown by medical helicopter to Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston and was reported to be in critical condition. Officials have not released his name, citing his privacy. The distinction matters because the public identification of Potter and Wolcott does not resolve the status of the hospitalized passenger or explain what led the boat into danger.

Wolcott’s status also changed in two ways over the course of Monday’s updates: authorities identified him, but he had not been found. The Coast Guard suspended its search Sunday, according to Boston.com and Boston 25. NBC Boston reported that Massachusetts State Police had aerial and marine units conducting additional searches Monday. The separate efforts should not be read as confirmation that Wolcott was located; the latest reports still described him as missing.

The dog was recovered alive and reunited with its family, according to the Coast Guard reporting cited by Boston.com and Boston 25. Boston 25 also reported that the vessel was salvaged with commercial assistance. Those details close out parts of the rescue operation while leaving the central questions unanswered: what caused the boat to lose control, how the men entered the water and what happened to Wolcott after the crash.

The incident remains under investigation by local and county authorities. The reports reviewed for this update do not announce an arrest, citation or completed marine investigation, and they do not assign responsibility for the crash. The Essex County District Attorney’s Office has said the inquiry is ongoing, so early descriptions of the rocks, the vessel’s movement and the initial 911 call should be kept separate from any eventual investigative finding.

For the North Shore, the case has required a coordinated response across neighboring harbors and state and federal agencies, reflecting the difficulty of searching active coastal waters from both land and air. The confirmed picture as of Monday afternoon was one death, one hospitalized man, one missing man and a surviving dog. Further information is most likely to come from the district attorney, Massachusetts State Police, the Coast Guard or local public-safety agencies as investigators continue documenting the crash and the search.
